title: argv arithmetic
prompt:
Every number on the command line gets added into one total. The args box under the editor holds four of them; change it and run again, and the output follows.

`main` receives `argc` in `x0` and `argv`, an array of string pointers, in `x1`. Entry zero is the program's own name, so start at one. Each entry is eight bytes, which is what the scaled form `ldr x0, [argv_r, i_r, lsl 3]` is for; `bl atoi` turns the string into a number.

Print the running total after each number is added, one per line, then the final total.

## what is checked

- the running totals and the final total for the args in the box
- the program exits cleanly
- the numbers come from argv (`atoi` called, total not written in)
- the same holds for other command lines you do not see, including one with no numbers at all
starter:
// add up every number handed to the program on its command line
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(argc_r, x19)
define(argv_r, x20)
define(i_r, x21)
define(total_r, x22)

        .data
fmt_step:   .string "%lld\n"
fmt_total:  .string "total = %lld\n"

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     argc_r, x0
        mov     argv_r, x1
        mov     total_r, 0
        mov     i_r, 1                      // argv[0] is the program name

        // TODO: loop from 1 to argc - 1. Each argv entry is a POINTER
        // to a string, eight bytes apart, so fetch it with
        // ldr x0, [argv_r, i_r, lsl 3], turn it into a number with
        // bl atoi, add the result into the total, and print the
        // running total with fmt_step.

        ldr     x0, =fmt_total
        mov     x1, total_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
